subsystem: Solana execution stack (compiler, owner-signed flow services, wallet signing, server broadcast, reconciliation, durable-nonce primitives)
summary: Every production Solana flow (Jupiter mainnet swap, SOL/SPL transfer, Orca Whirlpools liquidity, universal-router Relay deposit from Solana) follows one pattern: the server reads chain facts and compiles ONE exact v0 message itself with FloFi's dependency-free codec (packages/reference-compiler/src/solana.ts compileMessageV0:101-144, fee payer forced to static key 0 at 110/135) using a recent blockhash from getLatestBlockhash('confirmed'); simulates it with simulateTransaction (sigVerify false, replaceRecentBlockhash false; solana-swap.ts:109-118); freezes a Review whose commitment binds message, messageHash, blockhash and lastValidBlockHeight; on Execute the service persists a PREPARED attempt and claims the message hash BEFORE the wallet is asked (jupiter-service.ts:126-136); the BROWSER asks the owner's Wallet Standard wallet for `solana:signTransaction` of exactly one transaction (wallet/solana-wallet.ts signWithSolanaWallet:167-182, never sign-and-send); the server `submit` verifies the bytes are the reviewed message (or it plus verified Lighthouse assertions) with exactly one valid owner signature (solana-swap.ts verifySignedSolanaSwap:189-198, signatures.length !== 1 refused at 193), checks block-height validity, claims the signature, persists SUBMITTING, then broadcasts once with sendTransaction (base64, preflightCommitment confirmed, maxRetries 10; jupiter-service.ts:164-172). Workers only observe (their transports are wrapped by observeOnly, backend/app.ts:24-25, 73-88). Observation reads getBlockHeight('finalized') before getSignatureStatuses so absence past lastValidBlockHeight is definitive NOT_EXECUTED; reconciliation requires the finalized transaction to be byte-identical to the owner-signed bytes and measures owner deltas from meta pre/post (token) balances (reference-reconciler/src/jupiter.ts:40-135). Reconciled outputs flow into workflow runs through amountsFromOwnerRecord (workflow-runs/received-amounts.ts:27-113) and observeOwnerStep (workflow-runs/observe.ts:41-87). The owner is fee payer and sole signer in every flow; the only other signer anywhere in production flows is Orca OPEN's browser-generated, non-extractable WebCrypto position-mint key (wallet/position-mint-signer.ts:17-28), never a FloFi server key. No provider hands FloFi a prebuilt serialized transaction: Jupiter is called on Swap API v2 `/build` which returns instructions FloFi compiles (jupiter.ts:69-98, 221), and the Relay Solana deposit is rebuilt by FloFi and required to equal Relay's instruction byte-for-byte (relay-provider.ts:112-121). Hence every builder can be recompiled with a durable-nonce lifetime by swapping its compileMessageV0 call for solana-nonce.ts compileDurableNonceMessageV0:69-74 — but each flow's lifetime logic (review freshness `lastValidBlockHeight - 20`, submit staleness, EXPIRED observation by block height, policy nonce = lastValidBlockHeight) is hard-wired to recent blockhashes, and each builder's simulation requires the owner to already hold the step's input, which is impossible for steps pre-signed before a bridge delivers. Nothing implements multi-transaction signing (the browser destructures only the first result; FloFi Wallet refuses inputs.length !== 1), group submission, or nonce-lifetime observation yet; solana-nonce.ts is a tested pure primitive used by no product path.

answers.question: (1) Per Solana flow: fee payer, blockhash source, transactions per step, who signs, who submits; does any FloFi key co-sign?
answers.answer: Jupiter swap: fee payer = owner (compileMessageV0 payer arg = intent.owner; staticKeys[0] enforced); recent blockhash from the server's getLatestBlockhash({commitment:'confirmed'}) on the flow RPC (GRYLOO_SOLANA_RPC_URL or https://api.mainnet-beta.solana.com); exactly 1 transaction; signer = owner only (inspection refuses any other signer, verification refuses signatures.length !== 1); submitted by the FloFi server's sendTransaction on the browser's explicit submit. SOL/SPL transfer: same (owner payer, 'confirmed' recent blockhash, 1 tx, owner only, server broadcasts). Orca liquidity: owner payer, 'confirmed' recent blockhash, 1 tx per operation; signers = owner, plus for OPEN a browser-generated non-extractable single-use WebCrypto position-mint key that signs after the owner's wallet (its secret never reaches the server; it has no authority after the mint exists); server broadcasts. Universal bridge with Solana source: owner payer (route.depositor), 'confirmed' recent blockhash, 1 deposit tx (Relay steps other than one 'deposit' are refused), owner only, server broadcasts; delivery on the destination is made and paid by the Relay solver. Devnet swap->liquidity composition: 2 transactions, 2 prompts. No FloFi server key co-signs any production Solana transaction: every verifier pins the signer set (1 owner signature, or [owner, positionMint] for Orca OPEN). The only FloFi-controlled Solana signer anywhere is the MOCKED-harness delegated driver (session key as fee payer), which is refused in production (see delegation map).

answers.question: (2) What would it take to compile each flow with a durable-nonce lifetime; does any flow receive a prebuilt serialized tx from a provider that FloFi cannot rebuild?
answers.answer: No flow receives a prebuilt serialized transaction. Jupiter is called on Swap API v2 `/build`, which returns instruction objects (computeBudget, setup, swap, cleanup, ALT addresses) that FloFi validates and compiles itself; there is no `/swap` (serialized tx) or `/swap-instructions` call anywhere (grep). Relay's Solana deposit is rebuilt by FloFi and must equal Relay's single instruction; LI.FI and Mayan are discovery-only (not executable). Transfer and Orca instructions are FloFi-built. So mechanically each builder needs: (a) replace compileMessageV0(owner, ixs, blockhash, tables) with compileDurableNonceMessageV0(owner, nonce, ixs, tables) [jupiter.ts:221, solana-transfer.ts:244, orca-liquidity.ts:521, solana-chain.ts:97]; (b) prepend advanceNonceAccountInstruction to the instruction lists used by the round-trip asserts (assertMessageRoundTrip in jupiter.ts:225 / solana-transfer.ts:248, assertLiquidityMessageRoundTrip orca-liquidity.ts:303-316 and the review re-derivation at 700); (c) a Review lifetime discriminator {kind:'BLOCKHASH', lastValidBlockHeight} | {kind:'DURABLE_NONCE', nonceAccount, authority, nonce} replacing the block-height freshness checks (solana-swap.ts:174, solana-transfer.ts:348, prepareSolanaSwapAttempt executor/jupiter.ts:58, the services' submit staleness jupiter-service.ts:153, solana-transfer-service.ts:162, orca service 204, universal 572/861) with nonceStillValid on a fresh getMultipleAccounts read of the nonce account, and policy/manifest nonce fields (solana-swap.ts:149,152) bound to the nonce account+value; (d) EXPIRED observation by nonce advance instead of block height (solanaSwapObservationDecision executor/jupiter.ts:82-86, universal service.ts:593-599): definitive NOT_EXECUTED only when the finalized nonce account value differs from the signed one and the signature is absent; (e) size: the advance adds ~2 static keys + ~10 bytes (nonce account, RecentBlockhashes sysvar), so lower Jupiter maxAccounts (jupiter.ts:54) for nonce builds and keep the 1232-65 bound (solana.ts:154); keep the nonce account and sysvar static (compileMessageV0 may move a writable non-signer into an ALT, solana.ts:118-130). The real blocker is not compilation but preconditions: every builder refuses or fails simulation when the owner does not yet hold the step's input (jupiter.ts:216-217,232; solana-transfer.ts:175,200,207,280; orca-liquidity.ts:499; solana-chain.ts:90), and the standard RPC cannot simulate against a future post-bridge state, so a pre-signed post-bridge step cannot get the exact-message simulation FloFi's Review requires. Additionally Jupiter's swap data fixes in_amount, quoted_out_amount and slippage (decodeJupiterSwap jupiter.ts:101-110): the on-chain minimum stays enforced, but a stale route/price makes the delayed tx fail on chain (fee charged and, per Solana runtime rules not verified from repo source, nonce advanced). Transfer additionally uses getFeeForMessage (solana-transfer.ts:254) whose behaviour for nonce messages is not verified. Orca OPEN fixes liquidity from the pool price at simulate (orca-liquidity.ts:486-497) and needs the position-mint co-signature, which can be produced at pre-sign time in the same tab. A Solana-source Relay deposit is bound to a Relay order with a deadline, so it cannot usefully be pre-signed for a far-future time; it should be re-quoted when due.

answers.question: (3) How are Solana step outcomes reconciled and recorded so a dependent step can bind to them?
answers.answer: Each flow's observe(): getBlockHeight('finalized') first, then the reconciler: getSignatureStatuses([sig], {searchTransactionHistory:true}); only 'finalized' proceeds; getTransaction(sig, {encoding:'base64', commitment:'finalized', maxSupportedTransactionVersion:0}); the landed bytes must equal the owner-signed bytes (or the recorded Lighthouse guard re-verified); fee payer must be the owner; provider program present; fee <= reviewed estimate; owner deltas from meta.preBalances/postBalances and pre/postTokenBalances (native SOL on owner lamports with fee and created-account rent separated); minimum output enforced; no unrelated owner token movement. Swap observation stores inputSpent/outputReceived; transfer amountSent/amountReceived; Orca deposited/withdrawn effects; universal deposit ownerDebit and destination delivery amount (verifySolanaCredit = recipient's net credit in the mint within one finalized tx, order id checked as orderBound). The run record (journal + observations + evidence) is saved durably; the projector marks needsObservation/hasEvidence. Workflow runs: observeOwnerStep finds the step's flow runs by wallet and exact per-step workflow hash and takes amountsFromOwnerRecord(record) as StepOutcome.spent/received; confirm-mode bindings resolve min(cap, received) from that outcome. Native SOL uses the wrapped-mint asset key. Gaps: amountsFromOwnerRecord extracts nothing for Solana transfers (no review.output) and Orca liquidity (deposited/withdrawn not mapped), so neither can be a binding producer today; no Solana-side delivery can be 'final' before getTransaction finalized (verifyCredit sets final:true only after finalized read).

answers.question: (4) Which RPC methods/transport does the server use for Solana sends and reads, and where would a server-side sequential submitter for N owner-signed transactions plug in (attempt records, idempotency, blockhash expiry)?
answers.answer: Transport: createSolanaRpc(endpoint) — HTTPS JSON-RPC POST, one serialized queue per flow transport, 120 ms pacing (600 ms x attempt on retry) for non-loopback, 20 s timeout, 2 MB cap, up to 3 attempts on HTTP 429 except sendTransaction, JSON big-int lexeme preservation, allowlist: getGenesisHash, getSlot, getMultipleAccounts, getTokenAccountsByOwner, getLatestBlockhash, getBlockHeight, getFeeForMessage, simulateTransaction, getMinimumBalanceForRentExemption, getSignatureStatuses, getTransaction, sendTransaction (no getAccountInfo — nonce reads must use getMultipleAccounts, which is allowed). Endpoint GRYLOO_SOLANA_RPC_URL (https, no userinfo) or the profile default; the universal router builds its own instance. Sends: sendTransaction(signedBase64, {encoding:'base64', preflightCommitment:'confirmed', maxRetries:10}) only inside a service's submit(), reached from the browser's explicit submit API call; worker and preview transports wrap every RPC with observeOnly (WORKER_SUBMISSION_FORBIDDEN). Attempt records today: one attempt per run with states PREPARED -> SUBMITTING -> PENDING | SUBMISSION_RESULT_UNKNOWN -> CONFIRMED | REVERTED | EXPIRED | NOT_FOUND | RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED; idempotency by durable exclusive claims of messageHash (at begin) and owner signature (at submit) via solanaTransactionClaim, plus signature persisted before broadcast and 'never a second transaction' recovery by observation. Expiry: review/submit refuse at lastValidBlockHeight(-20); observation declares EXPIRED only when finalized height > lastValidBlockHeight and the signature is absent. Plug-in options for a sequential N-tx submitter: (A) browser-driven: after one sign-all prompt the browser calls a new group endpoint that runs each step-run's existing submit() in order, waiting for 'confirmed' (getSignatureStatuses) of k before submitting k+1; keeps the 'only explicit owner action sends' boundary and reuses every per-step claim/attempt/evidence; suitable for SOLANA_SIGN_ALL (all txs share a ~60-90 s blockhash window). (B) worker-driven: a new work kind (beside WORKFLOW_RUN_ADVANCE_KIND in workflow-runs/worker.ts:17) with a dedicated send-capable Solana transport that may only send bytes already verified and persisted on a group/step record; required for SOLANA_DURABLE_NONCE (broadcast when a bridge delivery reconciles, possibly with the browser closed); this relaxes the observeOnly boundary in backend/app.ts:73-88 for that kind only and must be an explicit, reviewed safety change with boundary tests. In both cases reuse: per-tx attempt state machine (executor/jupiter.ts:12-13), claims (solana-transaction-claim.ts), signature-before-send ordering (jupiter-service.ts:164-166), rebroadcast of the SAME bytes is idempotent (same signature) and safe while valid; on a recent-blockhash expiry of tx k, steps k..N become NOT_EXECUTED and the group fails closed (ask again with re-resolved amounts); on a nonce tx, validity is checked by reading the nonce account before each (re)broadcast and observation.

answers.question: (5) Concrete plan for SOLANA_SIGN_ALL and SOLANA_DURABLE_NONCE groups reusing existing builders, with exact files/functions to change.
answers.answer: Shared foundations: (i) compiler — add a lifetime parameter to every builder: type SolanaLifetime = {kind:'BLOCKHASH'} | {kind:'DURABLE_NONCE', account, authority, nonce, lamportsPerSignature}; in simulateJupiterSwap (jupiter.ts:203-255), simulateSolanaTransfer (solana-transfer.ts:234-296), simulateOrcaLiquidity (orca-liquidity.ts:471-563) and simulateSolanaDeposit (solana-chain.ts:82-126) choose compileMessageV0 vs solanaNonce.compileDurableNonceMessageV0, include the advance instruction in round-trip lists, record review.lifetime, and bind policy/manifest nonce to it (buildSolanaSwapArtifacts solana-swap.ts:121-161 and the transfer/orca artifact builders). (ii) review guards: assertSolanaSwapReview (solana-swap.ts:167-181), assertSolanaTransferReview (solana-transfer.ts:342-355), the Orca review assert (~690-700), prepareSolanaSwapAttempt (executor/jupiter.ts:54-65) and the services' submit staleness checks branch on lifetime. (iii) observation: solanaSwapObservationDecision (executor/jupiter.ts:82-86) and the transfer/universal equivalents gain a nonce branch: read nonce account (getMultipleAccounts, decodeNonceAccount) at finalized commitment BEFORE getSignatureStatuses; EXPIRED only if !nonceStillValid and signature absent. (iv) browser: add signAllWithSolanaWallet(session, unsigned[], prefix) in wallet/solana-wallet.ts beside signWithSolanaWallet (167-182): one feature.signTransaction(...inputs) call, results.length === inputs.length, each a <=1232-byte view, same session invalidation checks; Orca OPEN inputs get the position-mint signature per tx after the wallet returns (extend signOrcaLiquidityTransaction position-mint-signer.ts:41-55 to N). FloFi Wallet: flofi-solana-wallet.ts:89 refuses N inputs and managed-signing.ts binds one {flow, runId}; add a group binding (e.g. flow 'workflow-group') resolving each message to its step run's PREPARED attempt, or count N prompts honestly until Privy multi-sign is verified. SOLANA_SIGN_ALL (consecutive same-cluster steps, amounts fixed at signing): reuse one flow run per step; group service (new, e.g. apps/reference-dapp/src/workflow-runs/solana-group.ts + store rows in the planned workflow_run_groups table) does: simulate+review every step with amounts fixed (exact or the producer's guaranteed minimum, e.g. Jupiter quote.otherAmountThreshold jupiter.ts:76-77) -> begin() every step run (N PREPARED + message claims) -> return N unsignedTransaction -> one wallet prompt -> submitGroup: for k in 1..N call the step service's submit(runId_k, signed_k) (unchanged verification/claim/send), then poll getSignatureStatuses until 'confirmed' with err null before k+1; any refusal/expiry/revert stops the group (later attempts walletFailure -> CANCELLED, never sent). Restriction: a step whose input is produced by an earlier step of the same group cannot be simulated by the current builders (they require the input balance); either limit SIGN_ALL to steps whose inputs are already held (independent consecutive steps), or add a compiler 'pre-funded' mode that skips the balance precondition and relies on on-chain enforcement (TransferChecked exact amount, Jupiter minimum) — an explicit evidence downgrade — or compose dependent steps into ONE atomic transaction when it fits 1232 bytes (e.g. Jupiter swap + TransferChecked of the minimum output), which keeps exact simulation. SOLANA_DURABLE_NONCE (Solana steps after an EVM->Solana bridge): onboarding flow (new service + UI) creates N owner nonce accounts in one owner-paid tx; prefer CreateAccountWithSeed (System discriminator 3, present in installed @solana-program/system 0.16.0) so only the owner signs — solana-nonce.ts currently only has CreateAccount, which needs the new account's key; initialize with authority = owner; read with getMultipleAccounts + decodeNonceAccount. At authorization: compile each delayed step with lifetime DURABLE_NONCE and amount = the bridge route's guaranteed minimumOutput (min with cap), skip the balance precondition (explicitly typed as unsimulated-at-signing), include them in the same sign-all prompt as the immediate group, persist signed bytes + lifetime on the step run (PREPARED->SIGNED_HELD, a new state) without broadcasting. When the bridge's received is reconciled (service.ts:697) and received >= signed amount: worker (send-capable work kind) re-reads the nonce account (nonceStillValid), simulates the exact signed tx (simulateTransaction, sigVerify true), and only then calls the step service's submit path; failures before broadcast leave the bytes unsent and ask the owner to revoke (advanceNonceAccountInstruction self-tx) because FloFi cannot invalidate them. Retire nonce accounts with withdrawNonceAccountInstruction. implementationGuidance: Keep the existing per-step flow runs as the unit of review, attempt, claim, reconciliation and evidence; a Solana group should orchestrate N existing step runs (N begin() + one wallet prompt + ordered submit()) rather than invent a parallel transaction pipeline. This preserves observeOwnerStep/amountsFromOwnerRecord linkage (observe.ts:41-87) and every byte-exact verifier.

Add a lifetime discriminator to every Solana Review (BLOCKHASH vs DURABLE_NONCE {nonceAccount, authority, nonce}) and route all freshness/expiry decisions through one helper; today the block-height rule is duplicated in solana-swap.ts:174, solana-transfer.ts:348, executor/jupiter.ts:58,82-86, jupiter-service.ts:153,187, solana-transfer-service.ts:162,197, orca-liquidity-service.ts:204,238 and universal service.ts:572,593,861.

Build nonce messages only via solanaNonce.compileDurableNonceMessageV0 and verify landed/held bytes with durableNonceLifetimeOf; additionally assert the nonce account and RecentBlockhashes sysvar are static keys (compileMessageV0 can move writable non-signers into an ALT, solana.ts:118-130) and that the owner is fee payer = nonce authority.

Prefer CreateAccountWithSeed (System ix 3; codec present in installed @solana-program/system 0.16.0) for nonce-account onboarding so only the owner signs; if CreateAccount is kept, generate the nonce account key like position-mint-signer.ts (non-extractable, single use, browser only).

For Jupiter nonce builds, request /build with a lower maxAccounts (jupiter.ts:54) to leave room for the advance instruction (+2 static keys); keep parseJupiterBuild/inspectJupiterInstructions unchanged and prepend the advance instruction in jupiterInstructions/assertMessageRoundTrip.

Never pre-sign a dependent Solana step with an amount above the producer's guaranteed minimum (Jupiter otherAmountThreshold jupiter.ts:76-77; Relay route.minimumOutput). Before broadcasting a held step, require reconciled received >= signed amount (received-amounts.ts:57-70) and a fresh exact simulation; otherwise do not send and tell the owner to revoke by advancing the nonce.

Treat 'FloFi holds owner-signed bytes valid until the owner advances the nonce' as a disclosed standing capability (S10 honesty): show nonce accounts, held transactions and the one-click revocation (advanceNonceAccountInstruction self-tx) in the review; count onboarding (1 tx), sign-all prompts and revocations honestly.

Sequential SOLANA_SIGN_ALL submission must wait for 'confirmed' (not 'finalized') of tx k before submitting k+1 to fit the ~150-block blockhash window; reconciliation still requires finalized. If tx k expires or reverts, cancel k+1..N (walletFailure-style CANCELLED, never sent) and re-plan amounts from reconciled outcomes.

A worker that broadcasts held nonce transactions needs a send-capable transport for that work kind only; explicitly change and test the observeOnly boundary (backend/app.ts:23-25,73-88; backend/solana-cloud.pg.test.ts:51) and keep the gas-payer check (user-funded/gas-payer.ts assertUserFundedSubmission with kind SOLANA_TRANSACTION, feePayer = parsed staticKeys[0]) immediately before every sendTransaction.

Extend multi-tx signing in three places: wallet/solana-wallet.ts (new signAllWithSolanaWallet), wallet/position-mint-signer.ts (N Orca OPEN co-signatures), and FloFi Wallet (flofi-solana-wallet.ts:89 + managed-signing.ts group binding + flofi-privy-signer.ts) — the latter only after Privy multi-sign is verified; otherwise report N prompts for FloFi Wallet.
Extend received-amounts.ts so Solana transfers (spent) and Orca withdrawals (received A/B) become binding facts if they will be producers/consumers in groups.

Extend MOCKED chains (jupiter-mock.ts, solana-transfer-mock.ts, orca-mock.ts, universal.test-harness.ts) with nonce accounts, AdvanceNonceAccount, nonce-lifetime acceptance and nonce-advanced-on-failure semantics; extend the e2e mocked Wallet Standard wallet to sign all inputs and count one request.
gaps: No multi-transaction signing: signWithSolanaWallet uses only the first result (solana-wallet.ts:175); FloFi Wallet refuses inputs.length !== 1 (flofi-solana-wallet.ts:89); managed signing binds exactly one PREPARED attempt of one run (managed-signing.ts:263-280) and supports only jupiter-swap and solana-transfer for Solana (272-273), not Orca liquidity or universal deposits.
No group/sequential submitter; submit is one run per API call, and workers cannot send (backend/app.ts:23-25,73-88).

Durable nonce exists only as a pure primitive (solana-nonce.ts) with tests; no builder, review, attempt state, observation decision, onboarding flow, UI, config consumer or mock supports a nonce lifetime.
solana-nonce.ts lacks CreateAccountWithSeed and AuthorizeNonceAccount helpers; createNonceAccountInstruction requires the nonce account's own signature (33-37).

Builders cannot simulate steps whose input the owner does not yet hold (jupiter.ts:216-217,232; solana-transfer.ts:175-207,280; orca-liquidity.ts:499; solana-chain.ts:90); standard RPC offers no multi-tx/bundle or state-override simulation in the allowlist (solana-rpc.ts:5-6).
amountsFromOwnerRecord has no mapping for Solana transfer or Orca liquidity records (received-amounts.ts:27-113).
Policy/manifest 'nonce' fields carry lastValidBlockHeight (solana-swap.ts:149,152), not a durable lifetime.
Solana swap composition is Devnet-only (solana-composition.ts imports Devnet profiles 2-3; certification-matrix.ts:75-76); there is no mainnet multi-step Solana composition service.

risks: Pre-signed durable-nonce transactions are a standing capability: valid until the owner advances the nonce, and FloFi cannot revoke them; a leaked/replayed copy can be broadcast by anyone (still only the owner-signed effect, with the owner paying the fee).

Delayed Jupiter swaps bind a quoted route and minimum; price/route drift makes them fail on chain (fee lost; nonce consumed per Solana semantics, not verified from repo) or execute at the signed minimum — must be disclosed and pre-checked by simulation at broadcast time.

Pre-signed steps cannot get exact-message simulation at signing when inputs arrive later (bridge delivery or earlier group steps) — weakens the current 'simulate exact bytes before Review' invariant; needs an explicit, honest evidence level.

SOLANA_SIGN_ALL with recent blockhashes has a ~60-90 s window; slow confirmations or RPC rate limiting (serialized 120 ms paced queue) can expire later transactions, failing the group mid-way after earlier steps executed (partial execution must be reconciled and re-planned).

Wallet behaviour for N-input signTransaction (one prompt vs N, Lighthouse guard per tx, simulation of dependent later txs failing in the wallet UI) is unverified; Phantom-style prepended compute-budget changes would be refused (correctly) but break the group.
Making a worker able to send relaxes the observeOnly boundary; a bug there could broadcast held bytes at the wrong time (before delivery, after the owner cancelled in FloFi).
Transaction size: adding the advance instruction to Jupiter routes built with maxAccounts 64 can exceed 1232 bytes; Orca and transfer messages forbid ALTs (no headroom from tables).

One nonce account per held transaction; reusing an account for two held transactions makes one of them invalid; concurrent groups must lease nonce accounts exclusively (claim per nonce account+value).
Rent for nonce accounts (80 bytes; 1,447,680 lamports in the test fixture, solana-nonce.test.ts:11) is owner-funded and only refunded by an explicit withdraw; abandoned accounts lock owner SOL.
openQuestions: Should dependent consecutive Solana steps be composed into ONE atomic transaction (exact simulation, one signature) when they fit, instead of SOLANA_SIGN_ALL with unsimulatable later transactions?

Is a worker-side broadcaster for held owner-signed Solana bytes acceptable to the owner (boundary change), or must delayed Solana steps wait for the owner's browser to return (one more prompt-free click)?
Do mainnet RPC providers used in production accept getFeeForMessage/simulateTransaction for durable-nonce messages, and is a static (non-ALT) nonce account required?
Does the installed Privy SDK (3.51.0) support signing several Solana transactions in one confirmation (signAllTransactions)?
What deadline should FloFi apply to held nonce transactions (e.g. bridge deliveryAttentionSeconds 3600 from universal-router.ts:65) after which it refuses to broadcast and asks the owner to revoke?
Should Orca OPEN be allowed in delayed groups at all, given liquidity is fixed from the pool price at signing and requires the position-mint key to sign in the same tab?
